title: 2010 AMC12A 19
statement: Each of \(2010\) boxes in a line contains a single red marble, and for \(1 \le k \le 2010,\) the box in the \(k\)th position also contains \(k\) white marbles. Isabella begins at the first box and successively draws a single marble at random from each box, in order. She stops when she first draws a red marble. Let \(P(n)\) be the probability that Isabella stops after drawing exactly \(n\) marbles. What is the smallest value of \(n\) for which \(P(n) \lt \dfrac{1}{2010}?\)

solutions.text:
Since there are \(k + 1\) marbles in the \(k\) th box, there is a \(\dfrac{k}{k + 1}\) chance Isabella draws a white marble from it.

The probability of drawing a red marble is then \(\dfrac{1}{k + 1}.\) To stop after drawing the \(n\) th marble, the first \(n - 1\) marbles must have been white.

This happens with a probability of \[ \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{2}{3} \cdot \ldots \cdot \dfrac{n - 1}{n} \cdot \dfrac{1}{n + 1}. \]

Note that all the numerators cancel with the adjacent denominator, which means that this expression reduces to \(\dfrac{1}{n(n + 1)}.\)

We have to find the smallest \(n\) such that \[ \dfrac{1}{n(n + 1)} \lt \dfrac{1}{2010} \] \[ n(n + 1) \gt 2010. \]

Since \(44\cdot45=1980\lt2010\) but \(45\cdot46=2070\gt2010,\) the smallest such \(n\) is \(45.\)

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: The first \(n-1\) draws must be white, then the \(n\)th draw red
